# Book I, Proposition 40

*Equal triangles on equal bases*

> Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/40-idea.svg" alt="If two triangles on equal bases (red) are equal in area (yellow), the line through their tips runs parallel to the line of the bases (blue)." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>If two triangles on equal bases (red) are equal in area (yellow), the line through their tips runs parallel to the line of the bases (blue).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/40.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.40, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.

I say that they are also in the same parallels.

For let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BE.

For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]

But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.]

## In Lean

✅ Proved

From [`Elements/BookI/Prop40.lean`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop40.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments; the lines under each one are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop40 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hCDE : Triangle C D E)
    (hBCE : Between B C E) (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖C E‖) (heq : △ A B C = △ C D E)
    (hside : SameSideOf A D B E) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B E := by
  -- Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.
  have hBE : B ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hBCE
  obtain ⟨BE, hB, hE⟩ := Postulate1 B E hBE
  have hC : OnLine C BE := on_line_of_between_ends hBCE hB hE
  have hA_BE : ¬ OnLine A BE := hABC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hD_BE : ¬ OnLine D BE := hCDE.acb.off_line hC hE
  -- I say that they are also in the same parallels.
  -- For let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BE.
  -- For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`). F is where it
     meets CD, by I.30 (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBE⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BE
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hCDE.ne₁₂
  obtain ⟨F, hF_CD, hF_K⟩ :=
    Prop30.meet hKBE hC hC_CD (fun e => hD_BE (e ▸ hD_CD))
  have hF_BE : ¬ OnLine F BE := hKBE.not_onLine hF_K
  have hFCE : Triangle F C E := (Triangle.of_line hC hE hCDE.ne₁₃ hF_BE).cab
  obtain ⟨FE, hF_FE, hE_FE⟩ := Postulate1 F E hFCE.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC,
  -- CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]
  have h38 : △ A B C = △ F C E :=
    Prop38 hABC hFCE hbase ⟨K, BE, hKBE, hA_K, hF_K, hB, hC, hC, hE⟩
  -- But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also
  -- equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D C E = △ F C E :=
    CommonNotion1 ((area_bac C D E).symm.trans heq.symm) h38.symm
  /- F and D lie on the same side of CE, which is the straight line BE.
     Thus F lies on the ray from C through D. -/
  have hFD_side : SameSideOf F D C E :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hCDE.ne₁₃ hC hE
      (((SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB hE (hKBE.sameSide hF_K hA_K)).trans hside).sameSide hB hE)
  have hray : OnRay F C D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hFD_side ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hF_CD⟩ (fun e => hF_BE (e ▸ hC))
  /- Euclid's case has F between C and D; beyond D, DCE is the part and FCE
     the whole. Either way only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hFD : F = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hCDE.bac h1.symm
  -- Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.
  /- A parallel meeting CD away from D has been excluded: the parallel
     through A must pass through D itself. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hFD ▸ hF_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BE.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B E := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hBE hA_K hD_K hB hE hKBE
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar
  -- Q. E. D.]
```

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle `ABC` can be applied to the straight line `L` with `A` on `D`, `B` on the ray from `D` through `G`, and `C` on the side of `L` where `H` is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L22): Adding is associative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L25): Adding is commutative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L44): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L28): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L31): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L34): "Less than" is transitive. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L38): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)

## Mishnah

**An added converse.** The whole proposition stands in brackets, and Heath explains why: "Heiberg has proved by means of the papyrus-fragment mentioned in the last note that this proposition is an interpolation by some one who thought that there should be a proposition following I. 39 and related to it in the same way as I. 38 is related to I. 37, and I. 36 to I. 35" (vol. 1, p. 338). It is I.39's argument again, with the equal bases BC, CE for the one base, and I.38 for I.37.

**Where F falls.** Through A, I.31 draws the parallel to BE, and Euclid's F is where it meets CD. That it meets CD at all comes from I.30 (`Prop30.meet`): CD meets BE at C, so it meets the parallel to BE. I.38 makes ABC equal to FCE; our I.38 lets the bases share C and lets F be A, so neither needs a case of its own. Euclid names the given triangle CDE, then DCE, and `area_bac` says the two names give one area; Common Notion 1 makes DCE equal to FCE. So the certificate cites I.30 besides Euclid's I.31 and I.38, with Common Notions 1 and 5, and Postulate 5 comes in through I.29, by way of I.30 and I.38.

**"The greater to the less."** The same-side hypothesis puts F on the ray from C through D (`OnRay.of_sameSideOf`); I.39 says why it is needed. If CF is less than CD, FCE is part of DCE, and `area_lt_of_cut` makes it the less, by Common Notion 5; if CF is greater, DCE is the less, the case Proclus finds equally easy under I.39. So CF equals CD, F is D (`OnRay.eq_of_len_eq`), and the parallel through A is AD. Book Zero's `OnRay.eq_of_area_eq` makes this argument once, for I.39 too. Our figure draws the supposed case, with F between C and D and AF level; Heath draws AD level and AF sloping.

**The modern way.** Put BE on the x-axis. The bases have one length b, so a vertex at height y makes a triangle of area ½b|y|; equal areas give equal |y|, and the same side gives y the same sign. So A and D are at one height, and AD is parallel to BE.
